entities.name: Person:Patient
entities.description: A person receiving or registered to receive medical care, treatment, or undergoing examination.

entities.name: Person:Clinician
entities.description: A healthcare professional qualified in the clinical practice of medicine, such as a doctor, nurse, or surgeon.

entities.name: Person:Researcher
entities.description: A person who conducts scientific or medical research, clinical trials, or academic studies.

entities.name: Organization:Hospital
entities.description: An institution providing medical and surgical treatment and nursing care for sick or injured people.

entities.name: Organization:Pharma
entities.description: A commercial company or industry entity engaged in discovering, developing, manufacturing, and marketing drugs.

entities.name: Organization:Research-Inst
entities.description: An organization or academic center dedicated to scientific, medical, or clinical research and development.

entities.name: Disease:Infectious
entities.description: A disease caused by pathogenic microorganisms, such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, or fungi, that can be spread directly or indirectly.

entities.name: Disease:Chronic
entities.description: A human health condition or disease that is persistent or otherwise long-lasting in its effects (e.g., diabetes, hypertension).

entities.name: Disease:Neoplasm
entities.description: An abnormal mass of tissue that forms when cells grow and divide more than they should, including benign or malignant tumors (cancer).

entities.name: Disease:Genetic
entities.description: A health condition caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome, sequence, or chromosomes (e.g., Down syndrome, cystic fibrosis).

entities.name: Disease:Mental
entities.description: A wide range of mental health conditions or disorders that affect mood, thinking, and behavior (e.g., depression, schizophrenia).

entities.name: Symptom:Physical
entities.description: A physical manifestation of a disease or condition that is apparent to the patient (e.g., pain, fever, nausea, rash).

entities.name: Symptom:Psychological
entities.description: A mental, emotional, or behavioral manifestation experienced by the patient (e.g., anxiety, panic, hallucinations, mood swings).

entities.name: Anatomy:Organ
entities.description: A differentiated part of the body that performs a specific function, composed of multiple tissues (e.g., heart, liver, lungs).

entities.name: Anatomy:Body-Part
entities.description: A macroscopic external or internal structural region of the body (e.g., arm, chest, knee, abdomen).

entities.name: Anatomy:Cell-Tissue
entities.description: An ensemble of similar cells from the same origin that together carry out a specific function, or individual cellular structures.

entities.name: Biomarker:Gene
entities.description: A specific sequence of nucleotides in DNA or RNA that is located on a chromosome and functions as a biological marker.

entities.name: Biomarker:Protein
entities.description: A specific protein, peptide, or amino acid chain quantified or identified as an indicator of a biological or pathogenic state.

entities.name: Biomarker:Metabolite
entities.description: An intermediate or end product of metabolism tracked as a biological indicator in clinical samples.

entities.name: Treatment:Medication
entities.description: A substance or drug administered for medical treatment, prevention, or relief of a disease.

entities.name: Treatment:Surgery
entities.description: A medical technology consisting of a physical intervention on tissues or organs, involving incisions or closures.

entities.name: Treatment:Procedure
entities.description: A specific course of action or technique intended to achieve a medical result (e.g., intubation, dialysis, wound dressing).

entities.name: Treatment:Therapy
entities.description: A continuous remedial treatment of mental or physical disorders (e.g., physical therapy, radiation therapy, psychotherapy).

entities.name: Test:Lab-Test
entities.description: A medical procedure that involves testing a sample of blood, urine, or other substance from the body in a laboratory.

entities.name: Test:Imaging
entities.description: A technique and process of creating visual representations of the interior of a body for clinical analysis (e.g., X-ray, MRI, CT scan).

entities.name: Test:Biopsy
entities.description: The removal of a sample of tissue or cells from the body for examination under a microscope, typically to discover the presence or cause of a disease.

entities.name: Test:Genetic-Test
entities.description: A type of medical test that identifies changes in chromosomes, genes, or proteins to confirm or rule out a suspected genetic condition.

entities.name: Finding:Lab-Result
entities.description: The outcome, value, or recorded finding from a laboratory test (e.g., elevated WBC count, glucose level of 120 mg/dL).

entities.name: Finding:Imaging-Finding
entities.description: The descriptive outcome or abnormality observed in an imaging test (e.g., a 2cm nodule, fracture of the femur, tissue density).

entities.name: Finding:Clinical-Sign
entities.description: An objective evidence of disease noticed by a clinician during physical examination (e.g., high blood pressure, wheezing, jaundice).

entities.name: Substance:Drug
entities.description: A specific chemical substance or active pharmaceutical ingredient used to treat, cure, prevent, or diagnose a disease.

entities.name: Substance:Chemical
entities.description: Any distinct chemical element, compound, or molecule mentioned in a clinical context that is not directly classified as a standard therapeutic drug.

entities.name: Substance:Pathogen
entities.description: A bacterium, virus, or other microorganism that can cause disease in a host.

entities.name: Temporal:Date
entities.description: A specific point in time, calendar date, or year when a medical event occurred.

entities.name: Temporal:Duration
entities.description: The length or period of time during which a condition, symptom, or treatment persists (e.g., for 5 days, over 3 weeks).

entities.name: Temporal:Frequency
entities.description: The rate at which a medical event, dosage, or follow-up occurs or is repeated (e.g., twice daily, every 6 hours, weekly).

entities.name: Dosage
entities.description: The specified quantity or amount of a therapeutic agent prescribed or administered at one time or over a period.

entities.name: Route
entities.description: The path or method by which a drug, fluid, or other substance is taken into the body (e.g., oral, intravenous, topical).

entities.name: Severity
entities.description: The degree, intensity, or extent of a disease, symptom, injury, or triage priority (e.g., mild, severe, critical).

entities.name: Confidence
entities.description: The clinical certainty, probability, or status of a diagnosis or finding (e.g., suspected, confirmed, ruled out).

entities.name: Phase
entities.description: A specific stage in a clinical trial or disease progression framework (e.g., Phase III trial, terminal stage).

entities.name: Evidence-Level
entities.description: The grading or scientific validation strength behind a medical study, finding, or guideline evaluation.

entities.name: Disposition
entities.description: The final or planned status of a patient at discharge (e.g., transferred to home care, referred to rehab, self-care).

entities.name: Publication
entities.description: A reference to medical literature, scientific papers, journal publications, or official clinical reports.

entities.name: Location:Geopolitical
entities.description: A city, province, region, country, or geopolitical boundary (e.g., Hà Nội, Nghệ An, TPHCM, Việt Nam).

entities.name: Person:Health-Official
entities.description: A government official, policymaker, or administrative health leader (e.g., Minister of Health, Director of Health Department, hospital director).

entities.name: Organization:Health-Authority
entities.description: A government health agency, regulator, or administrative body (e.g., Ministry of Health 'Bộ Y tế', CDC, Department of Health 'Sở Y tế', WHO).

entities.name: Organization:Charity-Foundation
entities.description: A philanthropic trust, non-profit fund, or charity organization supporting healthcare initiatives (e.g., Quỹ Phenikaa vì trẻ em).

entities.name: Administrative:Position
entities.description: A professional title, job position, or rank in a healthcare or government institution (e.g., Giám đốc, Bộ trưởng, Trưởng khoa).

entities.name: Financial:Money
entities.description: A monetary value, currency amount, or budget allocation mentioned in clinical, research, or administrative health contexts (e.g., 30 tỷ đồng).

arguments.name: Patient
arguments.description: The individual patient who is the subject of the medical care, clinical encounter, or study population.

arguments.name: Clinician
arguments.description: The healthcare provider who orders, performs, interprets, or manages the clinical event.

arguments.name: Researcher
arguments.description: The scientist or investigator conducting a clinical trial or publishing a study finding.

arguments.name: Agent
arguments.description: The active entity, medical professional, or institution initiating or performing a procedure or transfer.

arguments.name: Institution
arguments.description: The hospital, clinic, pharmaceutical company, or research facility involved in or hosting the event.

arguments.name: Disease
arguments.description: The medical condition, pathology, or disorder being diagnosed, treated, or studied.

arguments.name: Symptom
arguments.description: The physical or psychological complaint experienced by the patient in relation to an event.

arguments.name: Anatomy
arguments.description: The body part, organ, or cell-tissue region targeted by a procedure, test, or injury.

arguments.name: Treatment
arguments.description: The specific intervention, medication, surgery, or therapy prescribed or administered.

arguments.name: Test
arguments.description: The laboratory, imaging, biopsy, or genetic test ordered or performed.

arguments.name: Finding
arguments.description: The concrete outcome, observation, lab value, or clinical sign reported from a test or examination.

arguments.name: Biomarker
arguments.description: The gene, protein, or metabolite discovered, analyzed, or extracted in a study finding.

arguments.name: Substance
arguments.description: The chemical compound, active drug, or pathogen involved in an interaction, administration, or trial.

arguments.name: Drug
arguments.description: The medication compound causing an adverse reaction, interaction, or overdose.

arguments.name: Reaction
arguments.description: The biological or clinical adverse event suffered by a patient due to a drug or treatment.

arguments.name: Trigger
arguments.description: The environmental factor, substance, pathogen, or concurrent disease that causes an onset or relapse.

arguments.name: Cause
arguments.description: The underlying disease, substance, or injury that led to an emergency visit, dosage change, or death.

arguments.name: Outcome
arguments.description: The post-surgical clinical results, signs, or lab values observed after an operation.

arguments.name: Effect
arguments.description: The specific clinical sign or physiological symptom caused by a drug-drug interaction.

arguments.name: Indication
arguments.description: The clinical sign, symptom, or disease justifying a drug approval or a test order.

arguments.name: Interpretation
arguments.description: The clinical judgment, concluding opinion, or diagnostic meaning extracted from a reported finding.

arguments.name: Time
arguments.description: The timestamp, date, duration, or frequency associated with the clinical or research event.

arguments.name: Place
arguments.description: The specific hospital ward, facility, or geographical location where the medical event occurs.

arguments.name: Dosage
arguments.description: The exact quantity, concentration, or volume of a substance administered or modified.

arguments.name: Route
arguments.description: The route of administration specified in a prescription or drug-delivery event.

arguments.name: Severity
arguments.description: The metric or level indicating how severe a symptom, worsening event, or reaction is.

arguments.name: Confidence
arguments.description: The diagnostic certainty or probability level of a given condition.

arguments.name: Disposition
arguments.description: The state or home/care arrangement assigned to a patient upon discharge.

arguments.name: Triage-Level
arguments.description: The priority or urgency tier assigned to a patient during an emergency visit.

arguments.name: Phase
arguments.description: The specific phase tier of a clinical trial being described.

arguments.name: Population
arguments.description: The cohort or group of patients being evaluated in a clinical trial or study.

arguments.name: Authority
arguments.description: The official regulatory body or expert institution approving a drug or treatment protocol.

arguments.name: Evidence-Level
arguments.description: The validated tier of scientific certainty behind a published study finding.

arguments.name: Publication
arguments.description: The specific journal, document, or written literature containing a study finding.

arguments.name: Old-Dose
arguments.description: The baseline or previous dosage level before a modification event.

arguments.name: New-Dose
arguments.description: The updated or target dosage level established after a modification event.

arguments.name: Gestational-Age
arguments.description: The duration of pregnancy calculated from the first day of the last menstrual period to the birth event.

arguments.name: Position
arguments.description: The administrative or professional job position/title involved in an appointment or role change.

arguments.name: Giver
arguments.description: The individual, company, or institution donating funds, grants, or resources to a healthcare initiative.

arguments.name: Recipient
arguments.description: The charity, foundation, hospital, or individual receiving donated funds or resources.

arguments.name: Money
arguments.description: The monetary value or currency amount representing project budgets, donations, or grants.

arguments.name: Target-Population
arguments.description: The specific cohort or demographic group of individuals targeted by a public health program or campaign (e.g., children under 6, pregnant women).

Clinical-Encounter:Admission.description: The formal act of accepting a patient into a hospital or healthcare facility for inpatient care.

Clinical-Encounter:Discharge.description: The official release of a patient from a hospital or clinic after a period of care or treatment.

Clinical-Encounter:Emergency-Visit.description: An unscheduled, urgent visit by a patient to an emergency department due to acute distress, injury, or severe illness.

Clinical-Encounter:Transfer.description: The relocation of a patient from one medical unit, department, or medical facility to another.

Clinical-Encounter:Follow-Up.description: A subsequent consultation or check-up appointment to monitor a patient's ongoing condition or post-treatment recovery.

Diagnosis:Diagnose.description: The process or act by a clinician to identify a specific disease, illness, or condition affecting a patient.

Diagnosis:Rule-Out.description: The clinical elimination of a prospective disease or diagnosis from consideration through testing or evaluation.

Diagnosis:Differential.description: The evaluation and listing of two or more alternative candidate diseases that could cause the observed clinical symptoms.

Diagnosis:Confirm.description: The establishing or definitive validation of a specific diagnosis based on conclusive tests or diagnostic findings.

Treatment-Event:Prescribe.description: The act of a clinician authorising or ordering a specific medication, procedure, or therapy plan for a patient.

Treatment-Event:Administer.description: The direct physical delivery or giving of a drug, treatment, or therapy to a patient by a clinician or healthcare professional.

Treatment-Event:Perform-Surgery.description: The execution of an operative surgical procedure on a patient's body structures to treat a pathological condition or injury.

Treatment-Event:Discontinue.description: The deliberate termination or permanent stopping of a drug regimen, surgery protocol, or continuous therapy.

Treatment-Event:Modify-Dosage.description: The act of changing (increasing, decreasing, or adjusting) the quantity, volume, or timeline of an ongoing medication regimen.

Disease-Progression:Onset.description: The initial appearance, manifestation, or beginning point of a disease, clinical condition, or patient symptom.

Disease-Progression:Worsen.description: An increase in severity, deterioration, or exacerbation of an existing disease state or acute symptoms.

Disease-Progression:Improve.description: The visible amelioration, decrease in severity, or positive recovery trend of a medical condition or disease.

Disease-Progression:Remission.description: A structural or temporary period during which the symptoms and clinical indicators of a disease (especially cancer or chronic illnesses) disappear or significantly decrease.

Disease-Progression:Relapse.description: The return, recurrence, or deterioration of a disease or clinical symptoms after a temporary period of improvement or remission.

Disease-Progression:Death.description: The cessation of all biological functions that sustain a living organism, caused by a disease, complication, or toxic substance.

Examination:Order-Test.description: The administrative or clinical directive given by a clinician requesting a laboratory, imaging, or specific screening test for a patient.

Examination:Perform-Test.description: The actual physical or laboratory execution of a medical test, imaging capture, or cellular sampling on a patient.

Examination:Report-Finding.description: The communication, writing down, or structural release of lab results, imaging data, or clinical evaluations identified from a test.

Medication-Event:Adverse-Reaction.description: The development of an unwanted, harmful, or negative symptom or physiological response caused by the normal administration of a drug.

Medication-Event:Drug-Interaction.description: A physiological or clinical outcome resulting from the chemical or pharmaceutical intersection of a drug with another drug, food, or chemical compound.

Medication-Event:Overdose.description: The ingestion or administration of a dose of a drug or chemical substance that is significantly larger than recommended, causing acute toxicity or critical harm.

Research:Clinical-Trial.description: A structured research study involving human volunteers to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and clinical endpoints of a medical intervention or drug.

Research:Drug-Approval.description: The official decision or granting of permission by a regulatory authority to market and distribute a pharmaceutical drug for specific clinical indications.

Research:Study-Finding.description: The published or announced scientific conclusion, biological extraction, or statistical discovery resulting from medical or laboratory research.

Life-Event:Birth.description: The emergence of a baby or neonate from the body of its mother, including the entry into a clinical recording system.

Life-Event:Injury.description: Physiological damage or trauma inflicted on a patient's body due to external factors, accidents, or force.

Facility-Event:Launch.description: The official opening, inauguration, deployment, or launch of a new medical facility, hospital branch, clinical department, or center.

Personnel:Appoint.description: The formal appointment, hiring, promotion, or transfer of a clinician or official to a healthcare leadership or administrative role.

Public-Health:Campaign.description: A public health campaign, national medical program, vaccination drive, or community-wide health initiative.

Financial-Event:Donation.description: A philanthropic donation, funding grant, or budget allocation to support medical treatments, facilities, research, or community health initiatives.

Medical-Incident:Adverse-Event.description: A medical error, malpractice incident, procedural complication, or regulatory infraction involving unlicensed clinics or clinical neglect resulting in patient harm/death.

Medical-Incident:Violent-Assault.description: An act of violence, physical or verbal assault, or major security breach directed at healthcare workers or medical staff within a facility.

Public-Health:Outbreak.description: A regional outbreak, community transmission, or sudden local spike of an infectious disease within a community.

Supply-Chain:Shortage.description: The sudden shortage, depletion, or unavailability of essential pharmaceutical drugs, vaccines, or critical medical equipment.

Treatment-Event:Successful-Rescue.description: A highly successful, critical, or pioneering medical intervention where medical staff save a patient's life from near-fatal arrest, trauma, or complex disease.
